The API provides paid voice services, including speech-to-speech pricing of **$0.08 per minute**, batch speech-to-text at **$0.10 per hour**, streaming speech-to-text at **$0.20 per hour**, and text-to-speech at **$15 per one million characters**.[4][9] API rate limits depend on team tier and include requests-per-second and concurrent-session limits for voice/audio endpoints.[5]

- Extra usage credits and plan upgrades are available after reaching the weekly allowance.[1][2]

- Keep status as **GA** for consumer Grok Voice.
- Retain the regional rule, rewritten as **available where X/Grok is supported**, rather than “globally” without qualification.
- Add the official product URL: **x.ai/grok**.

OpenAI now directs users to **ChatGPT Work** (launched July 9, 2026) for longer, multi-step tasks, research, actions across apps/files, and finished deliverables like spreadsheets, slides, or reports.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent)[[2]](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/)

### Key Official Sources
- OpenAI Help Center article on ChatGPT agent (updated ~27 days before Oct 12, 2026): Explicitly states at the top, “ChatGPT agent is no longer available. Use ChatGPT Work...” while retaining older details on plans/limits (which are now superseded). It previously covered availability on Pro/Plus/Business/Enterprise/Edu plans in supported countries, with the noted monthly message limits (initial requests only), and support on web, iOS/Android mobile apps, and macOS/Windows desktop apps.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent)
- OpenAI announcement on introducing ChatGPT agent (July 17, 2025, with later updates noting it is outdated): Launched as a unified agentic system (combining elements of Operator and deep research) via “agent mode” in the tools dropdown. Rolled out starting with Pro/Plus/Team (later Enterprise/Edu), with Pro at 400 messages/month and others at 40.[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent)[[4]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/)
- Related pages on ChatGPT Work and cloud browser workflows confirm the shift.[[2]](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/)

### Recent Changes (Last 30–60 Days, ~Aug–Oct 2026)
- **Deprecation**: Agent mode was retired around early August 2026. The help center was updated with the “no longer available” notice (and redirection to ChatGPT Work or cloud browser features). Older documentation and limits remain visible but are overridden.[[5]](https://rottenwifi.com/chatgpt-agent-availability-and-price-what-happened-and-what-replaced-it/)[[6]](https://www.sentisight.ai/what-is-chatgpt-agent-beginners-guide/)
- No new pricing/tier changes, plan expansions, or restrictions announced specifically for the old Agent Mode in this period. ChatGPT Work follows similar paid-plan gating (Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise/Edu) but uses different metering (e.g., Codex-style allowances or credits in some cases) and focuses on goal-oriented, longer-running tasks.[[7]](https://justinmckelvey.com/blog/chatgpt-work)
- **Platforms**: No major updates noted; historical support aligned with web (chatgpt.com), mobile apps, and desktop apps. API-related agent capabilities exist separately (e.g., Agents API in public beta as of Sept 2026).[[8]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-agents-api/)
- **Regional/Other**: Rollout had earlier limitations (e.g., EEA/Switzerland phased); no new country-specific announcements in the recent window. Enterprise/Edu workspaces had admin toggles and controls.
- **X (@OpenAI)**: Recent searches primarily surface 2025 preview announcements; no new posts about Agent Mode status or changes in the results.[[9]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/1984304194837528864)

### Current Availability Summary
- **Status**: Deprecated/GA feature retired; replaced by ChatGPT Work (and related tools like cloud browser in ChatGPT).
- **Plans**: Old Agent Mode limits/availability no longer apply. ChatGPT Work is available on paid plans (Plus and above), with Free/Go excluded.
- **Platforms**: Web, mobile (iOS/Android), desktop apps (Windows/macOS); not Linux, standalone Chrome extension, or terminal in the documented sense.
- **Notes**: Tasks in the successor features emphasize user control, approvals for actions, connectors/apps, and safety measures. Usage is subject to plan-specific limits/credits and rate limits.

The stored data accurately reflected the feature around its 2025 launch/early rollout but does not account for the August 2026 deprecation and replacement. For the latest, refer directly to the OpenAI Help Center article on ChatGPT agent (which now redirects) and ChatGPT Work documentation.

**Stored data: INCORRECT — changes required.**

| **Free** | ✅ Available | Limited usage, subject to capacity and limits; users may need to wait or upgrade after reaching a limit.[2] |

| **Microsoft 365 Premium** | ✅ Available | Extensive Chat usage and higher limits for several AI features; includes advanced features such as Researcher and Analyst.[1][14] |
| **Microsoft 365 Copilot** | ✅ Available | Commercial Copilot Chat is available to users with qualifying Microsoft 365 licenses, with availability depending on the organization’s licensing and configuration.[1][10] |

Specific changes from the stored record:

- The **Free** tier is not accurately characterized simply as “Standard.” Microsoft describes it as a **limited free version subject to available capacity and limits**.[2]
- Microsoft 365 Personal and Family are documented as having **extensive Chat usage**, rather than merely “extensive use” without qualification.[14]
- Microsoft 365 Premium provides higher limits and exclusive features, including **Researcher and Analyst**.[1][14]
- The stored plan label **“M365 Copilot”** should preferably be updated to **“Microsoft 365 Copilot”**.
- Microsoft’s current pricing material also references **Microsoft 365 Pro**, which is absent from the stored list; it is not one of the plans requested, but the database should account for it if it tracks all current Copilot tiers.[2][6]

The stored availability checkmarks are otherwise correct for the five requested plans.

**The stored data on Microsoft Copilot's "Chat" feature remains accurate as of October 2026, with no major changes identified in pricing/gating, core platform availability, feature status (still GA), or regional restrictions in the last 30-60 days.**[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/overview)[[2]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/enterprise)

Official Microsoft documentation (primarily focused on the enterprise/work "Microsoft Copilot Chat" or "M365 Copilot Chat" experience, which aligns closely with the described "Chat" feature) consistently describes it as a secure, web-grounded AI chat experience included at no additional cost with eligible Microsoft 365 subscriptions. It is distinct from the paid Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license, which provides priority access, deeper work-data grounding (via Microsoft Graph), and advanced agents.[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/overview)[[3]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/how-copilot-chat-works-with-and-without-a-microsoft-365-copilot-license-5810b659-fbe0-48ee-9fe6-d731fe86cdeb)[[2]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/enterprise)

### Key Confirmations from Official Sources
- **Pricing/Plans and Gating (Free/Included)**: Copilot Chat (Basic) is available at no extra cost for users with eligible M365 subscriptions (work/school accounts via Entra ID). Consumer/personal plans (e.g., Free tier with basic access, Microsoft 365 Personal/Family, or Premium) align with the stored notes on sign-in requirements for history/longer sessions/image/voice features. M365 Copilot add-on provides "Premium"/priority access and extras like advanced agents (Researcher/Analyst). No recent pricing changes or new restrictions were announced for the base Chat feature.[[2]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/enterprise)[[4]](https://www.microsoft.com/en/microsoft-365-copilot/chat)
- **Platforms**: Matches the stored data closely. Access via web (copilot.microsoft.com or redirects to m365.cloud.microsoft/chat), Microsoft Copilot app (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android), and Edge sidebar. No native Linux app or dedicated consumer API for Chat (enterprise APIs are separate). Browser support (including Chrome for the web version) is confirmed, though some side-pane experiences are Edge-specific.[[5]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/download-copilot-app)[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/overview)[[6]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/manage)
- **Status**: Remains generally available (GA). It is the baseline "standalone" experience; recent updates (e.g., September/October 2026) focus on enhancements like better integrations, Copilot Pages, agents (metered), refreshed designs in apps like Teams/Outlook, and new capabilities (e.g., Home experience in the Copilot app), but do not alter the core GA status or availability of Chat itself.[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/overview)[[7]](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-copilot-blog/what%e2%80%99s-new-in-microsoft-copilot--september-2026/4559107)
- **Regional Availability**: Available in many regions worldwide, with some market restrictions possible (escalation options noted in docs). No new country rollouts or broad restrictions announced recently.[[8]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/faq)
- **Recent Changes (Last 30-60 Days)**: September/October 2026 updates emphasize enterprise enhancements (e.g., new Home/Cowork/Code/Autopilot experiences rolling out via Frontier program, Fabric IQ/Work IQ integrations, design refreshes, and agent/skills improvements). These build on Chat without changing its fundamental free/GA nature or platform support. Some older redirects (e.g., copilot.cloud.microsoft) were noted in prior years. No deprecations or major consumer-side shifts.[[7]](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-copilot-blog/what%e2%80%99s-new-in-microsoft-copilot--september-2026/4559107)[[9]](https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2026/09/25/introducing-the-new-copilot-with-home-code-and-autopilot/)

**Summary of Current Availability**: The feature is widely accessible as described—free/included for eligible plans with standard or priority limits depending on licensing, on the listed platforms (web + apps for Windows/macOS/mobile; no Linux/terminal/consumer API). It supports web grounding, file uploads, image creation, and more, with sign-in enhancing the experience. Enterprise docs highlight its role as the entry point before adding M365 Copilot.[[3]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/how-copilot-chat-works-with-and-without-a-microsoft-365-copilot-license-5810b659-fbe0-48ee-9fe6-d731fe86cdeb)[[6]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/manage)

Official sources used include Microsoft Learn documentation (e.g., Copilot overview and requirements pages), Microsoft Support articles on licensing differences, Microsoft 365 pricing/enterprise pages, and related blog/release notes. No conflicting information was found on X from official accounts in targeted recent searches. If consumer-specific personal Copilot (vs. work M365 Chat) details differ slightly in edge cases, the stored data aligns well with publicly described experiences.

Official Microsoft pages confirm the tiered availability for consumer Microsoft 365 plans (Personal, Family, Premium) and the commercial M365 Copilot add-on, along with the listed platforms. Copilot integrates into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and OneNote (with some market/licensing variations noted).[[3]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/in-apps-for-work)[[3]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/in-apps-for-work)

### Key Confirmations from Official Sources
- **Consumer plans (Personal/Family/Premium)**: Copilot is available in the desktop/web/mobile versions of the Office apps for the subscription owner (with AI credits/per-feature limits that increase with higher tiers like Premium). Free tier is limited to web/app chat without Office app integration. Family shares storage/apps but restricts Copilot AI benefits to the owner.[[1]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot-for-microsoft-365)[[2]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/individuals)[[2]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/individuals)
- **Commercial (M365 Copilot add-on)**: Requires a qualifying base Microsoft 365 plan (e.g., Business Basic/Standard/Premium, E3/E5, etc.) and provides full/enterprise features, including deeper work-data grounding.[[4]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/microsoft-365-copilot-licensing)[[4]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/microsoft-365-copilot-licensing)
- **Platforms**: Supported on Windows and macOS desktop apps, iOS/Android mobile apps, and web (Office on the web). Not available on Linux, ChromeOS (or similar), terminal, or via consumer API. A separate Microsoft 365 Copilot app (formerly tied to Office) is available on supported platforms.[[3]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/in-apps-for-work)[[5]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/download-copilot-app)[[3]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/in-apps-for-work)
- **Status**: Generally available (GA) with the described gating. Copilot Chat (lighter version) has broader/no-extra-cost access for eligible M365 subscribers in some contexts, but full in-app Copilot experiences align with the paid tiers in the stored data.[[6]](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftmechanicsblog/copilot-now-included-with-word-excel-powerpoint-outlook--onenote--microsoft-365-/4458434)

**The stored data remains largely accurate based on official Microsoft sources as of October 2026, with no major discrepancies or recent changes identified in the last 30-60 days.**[[1]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ai-credits-and-limits-for-microsoft-365-subscriptions-68530f1a-4459-4d02-9818-8233c1f673b8)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)

Key confirmations and details from official pages (primarily Microsoft Support and Copilot documentation):

- **Pricing/gating and availability by plan**: Copilot Vision requires a qualifying subscription for personal accounts (Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, or Premium) or a Microsoft Copilot license for work/school accounts. Free users are not listed as having access in the official limits documentation. Exact daily usage limits match the stored data precisely: 10 minutes/day for Personal and Family; 15 minutes/day for Premium. Commercial users have per-license access. These are feature-specific limits (separate from broader AI credits).[[1]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ai-credits-and-limits-for-microsoft-365-subscriptions-68530f1a-4459-4d02-9818-8233c1f673b8)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)

- **Platforms and notes**: Matches closely—available on Windows (screen/app sharing), macOS (via native app or supported paths), iOS/Android (Copilot mobile app, including camera), and Edge (in-browser). Not available on Linux, Chrome, terminal, or consumer API. Web access is noted for commercial/Entra ID users. Mobile screen/camera sharing and Windows app/window sharing are explicitly supported.[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)

- **Status**: The feature is available and in active rollout/expansion (described as available in supported regions/languages, with some notes on gradual enablement or varying availability during rollout). It is not presented as beta/preview-only in current consumer support docs, aligning with the stored "ga" status. Privacy notes emphasize no training use of session data and session deletion.[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)

- **Regional availability**: Available in supported regions (with US as a primary/early market and ongoing rollouts to more markets; some older notes mention US exceptions like Illinois/Texas). No new country-specific restrictions or major expansions detailed in recent official pages.[[3]](https://copilot.microsoft.com/labs/experiments/copilot-vision)

- **Recent changes (last 30-60 days)**: No announcements of pricing changes, new tiers, plan restrictions, deprecation, or significant platform/API updates appear in official Microsoft Support, Copilot blog/docs, or recent posts from @MSFTCopilot. Rollouts (e.g., to additional Windows/mobile users or markets) have been ongoing since earlier in 2025–2026, but the core availability, limits, and gating described in the stored data align with current documentation.[[4]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/2025/06/25/release-notes-june-25-2025/)

**Summary of current availability**: Copilot Vision is a subscription-gated feature (paid plans required for personal use; commercial licenses for work accounts) with the exact per-plan daily time limits noted in the stored data. It supports screen sharing on desktop (Windows/macOS/Edge/web for commercial) and camera on mobile apps, with strong privacy controls. It is generally available in supported regions but subject to rollout variations. The stored data accurately reflects official details from Microsoft Support pages on usage, limits, and access.[[1]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ai-credits-and-limits-for-microsoft-365-subscriptions-68530f1a-4459-4d02-9818-8233c1f673b8)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-vision-with-microsoft-copilot-3c67686f-fa97-40f6-8a3e-0e45265d425f)

**Primary sources cited**: Microsoft Support articles on using Copilot Vision and AI credits/limits for Microsoft 365 subscriptions; Copilot Labs/experiments page. No conflicting official information was found.

**The stored data on Copilot Voice remains accurate based on current official Microsoft sources (as of October 2026).** No significant changes were identified in pricing/tiers, limits, platform support, feature status (still GA), or regional availability in the last 30-60 days.[[1]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ai-credits-and-limits-for-microsoft-365-subscriptions-68530f1a-4459-4d02-9818-8233c1f673b8)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-voice-with-microsoft-copilot-efad42fc-d593-49c6-98bf-5ed94c881c32)

### Key Confirmations from Official Sources
- **Pricing, gating, and limits (consumer tiers)**: Free users have access subject to capacity (no priority during constraints). Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers get 30 minutes/day with priority access. Microsoft 365 Premium (top consumer tier) gets 60 minutes/day with priority. AI benefits apply only to the subscription owner. These match the stored data exactly.[[1]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/ai-credits-and-limits-for-microsoft-365-subscriptions-68530f1a-4459-4d02-9818-8233c1f673b8)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-voice-with-microsoft-copilot-efad42fc-d593-49c6-98bf-5ed94c881c32)
  - Sources: Microsoft Support “AI credits and limits for Microsoft 365 subscriptions” (updated/referenced in 2026) and “Using Copilot Voice with Microsoft Copilot.”
- **Platforms**: Available on web (copilot.microsoft.com with microphone), Windows (native integration/Copilot key/app), macOS (Copilot app), iOS/Android (Copilot apps), and Edge. Not available natively on Linux (web only), Chrome extension (not mentioned), terminal, or public consumer voice API. This aligns with the stored data.[[3]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/for-individuals/do-more-with-ai/general-ai/what-is-copilot-voice/)[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-voice-with-microsoft-copilot-efad42fc-d593-49c6-98bf-5ed94c881c32)
- **Status**: Generally available (GA) for Copilot Voice (real-time spoken conversations). Expanded rollout completed in phases through 2025–early 2026 (mobile first, then desktop/web).[[4]](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-copilot-blog/voice-turns-microsoft-365-copilot-into-your-thought-partner-/4469040)[[5]](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoft-copilot-blog/introducing-voice-in-microsoft-365-copilot-a-more-productive-way-to-work-on-the-/4466034)
- **Other notes**: Voice works across personal and work/school accounts (with differences in grounding/data handling). Supported in a growing set of languages/regions (availability can vary). No public mentions of new country rollouts or restrictions in recent official docs.[[2]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/using-copilot-voice-with-microsoft-copilot-efad42fc-d593-49c6-98bf-5ed94c881c32)

### Recent Changes (Last 30–60 Days or Notable 2026 Updates)
- No updates to limits, tiers, or core availability/pricing for consumer Copilot Voice.
- In August 2026, the animated Mico character was removed from Copilot Voice (moved to Learn Live); voice functionality itself continues unchanged.[[6]](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/08/14/less-than-a-year-on-microsoft-tells-mico-to-pipe-down/5287793)[[7]](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-copilot/frequently-asked-questions-about-retired-copilot-features)
- Broader context (earlier 2025–2026): Free/unlimited access to Voice was announced/rolled out for all users (with paid tiers retaining priority/higher effective use); work-focused voice expansions (e.g., Microsoft 365 Copilot app) reached GA. Limits pages confirm the current per-day caps with priority for paid plans.[[8]](https://microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/blog/2025/02/25/announcing-free-unlimited-access-to-think-deeper-and-voice)
- No relevant recent posts from the official @MSFTCopilot X account on Voice specifics in the searched results.

**Overall summary**: Copilot Voice is GA, widely available on major consumer platforms (web + apps on Windows/macOS/mobile), gated by subscription with the exact limits and priority rules listed in the stored data. Free access exists but is capacity-constrained; paid M365 tiers provide defined daily minutes and priority. No material deviations or recent shifts were found in official Microsoft pricing, support, or documentation pages.

| Microsoft 365 Family | Available | Similar to Personal; AI benefits are available to the subscription owner and are not shared with other Family members.[1][3] |
| Microsoft 365 Premium | Available | Higher or extensive limits, exclusive advanced features, and access to agents such as Researcher and Analyst.[3][5] |
| Microsoft 365 Copilot | Available for eligible organizational users | Model selection is supported in the Microsoft 365 Copilot experience; organizational licensing and administrator configuration apply.[7] |
| Microsoft 365 Pro | Also documented | Microsoft’s current comparison and limits documentation lists Pro separately, with the highest usage levels for several features.[3][4] |

**Pricing, tiers, and limits (Google One / Gemini Apps plans):**  
- **Free**: Limited access (e.g., ~5 reports/month in some descriptions; Flash/Fast/Thinking model only; subject to daily/concurrent request caps and high-demand restrictions).[[3]](https://www.ai-toolbox.co/gemini-management-and-productivity/gemini-usage-limits-2026)[[4]](https://www.stackaible.com/tools/gemini)

- **Google AI Pro** ($19.99/mo): 4x higher limits than Free / expanded access; full Pro model for higher-quality reports.[[6]](https://one.google.com/about/google-ai-plans/)

As of **October 12, 2026**, the stored record is **substantially incorrect**: Google no longer presents “Gemini Advanced” as a deprecated, paid-only product. The current product is presented through **Gemini Apps** and **Google AI plans**, including **AI Plus, AI Pro, and AI Ultra**.

## 1. Pricing-tier availability

**Stored data: INCORRECT.**

Google’s current limits page lists these tiers:

| Plan | Gemini Apps access |
|---|---|
| Free / without an AI plan | Standard limits |
| Google AI Plus | 2× standard limits |
| Google AI Pro | 4× standard limits |
| Google AI Ultra | 5× or 20× AI Pro limits, depending on the subscription |
| Workspace | Separate Workspace-specific availability and limits |

Usage is not a single fixed message quota. Google says limits depend on prompt complexity, the model or feature used, and conversation length. Limits refresh every five hours until a weekly limit is reached.[1]

The stored record should be changed as follows:

- **“Gemini Advanced”** should not be treated as a separate current paid tier.
- **Google AI Plus** is missing and provides approximately **2× Free usage limits**.[1]
- **Google AI Pro** provides approximately **4× Free usage limits**, not “full” unlimited access.[1]
- **Google AI Ultra** provides **5× or 20× Pro limits**, depending on the Ultra subscription.[1][9]
- The Free tier has standard or varying limits, rather than access described specifically as “varying access to 3.1 Pro.”[1]
- Workspace accounts have separate product and edition-based limits; Google’s Workspace documentation says availability varies by Workspace plan.[2][5]

Google’s current product page also describes AI Plus as offering 2× Free usage, while Ultra tiers offer 5× or 20× Pro usage limits and additional features such as Deep Think in selected countries.[9]

## 2. Platform and surface availability

**Stored data: INCORRECT.**

The current Gemini experience is available through the following surfaces:

| Surface | Current status |
|---|---|
| Windows | Available through the web app; no separate Windows-native “Gemini Advanced” product identified |
| macOS | Available through the web app; no separate macOS-native product identified |
| Linux | Available through the web app |
| iOS | Available through the Gemini mobile app |
| Android | Available through the Gemini mobile app, with Android-specific integration |
| Web | Available at Gemini’s web app |
| Terminal | Not established as a Gemini Apps surface; separate developer tools may exist |
| API | Available through the Gemini API, but this is a separate developer product rather than the consumer “Gemini Advanced” subscription |

The record’s Linux entry is specifically wrong: a web-based service is not restricted by operating system, so Linux users can access Gemini through a supported browser. Conversely, “API: available” should not be used as evidence that the consumer Gemini Advanced feature is available through the API; API access is separately provisioned and metered.

Google states that Gemini Apps usage across devices—including the web app, mobile app, and Gemini in Chrome—counts toward the applicable limits.[2] Google’s Workspace documentation also identifies Gemini web and mobile access, while noting that availability depends on the account and Workspace edition.[2][5]

## 3. Current status

**Stored status: INCORRECT.**

The current consumer product is **active and generally available**, subject to regional rollout, account eligibility, plan limits, and feature-specific availability. It is not accurately classified as **deprecated**.

Google’s current Gemini pages describe active rollout of Gemini 3.1 Pro and continued access for AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers.[15] The current Google AI plan page remains active and describes available subscription benefits.[9]

The name **“Gemini Advanced”** is best treated as a legacy product label or historical naming convention, not as a deprecated feature whose functionality has been discontinued. Google’s current product pages instead emphasize Gemini Apps and Google AI plans.

## 4. Access gating

**Stored gating: PARTIALLY CORRECT, but incomplete.**

Access is **mixed**, not simply paid-only:

- Basic Gemini access is available on the Free tier.
- Higher usage limits and premium models/features are gated by Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscriptions.
- Workspace access may be gated by an eligible organization’s Workspace edition or add-on.
- Some features have age, country, account, or plan restrictions.

Google explicitly lists “without an AI plan” as a supported tier with standard limits, so the overall Gemini service is not paid-only.[1] Paid plans provide expanded access and higher limits, while Google AI Ultra provides the highest access.[1][12]

The database should replace `gating: "paid"` with something such as **“free with paid upgrades; Workspace features may be org-gated.”**

## 5. Regional availability

**Stored regional note: PARTIALLY CORRECT.**

Gemini Apps and Google AI plans are available in many countries, but availability is not globally uniform. Google’s documentation says plan use is subject to country-specific availability and age requirements; in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom, users generally must be at least 18 to use Gemini Apps with a Google AI plan.[1]

Google also identifies feature-specific exclusions. For example, Gemini Spark is listed as unavailable in the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.[8] Google’s business documentation says Google AI Ultra for Business is available in more than 150 countries and territories, which also indicates broad—but not universal—availability.[2]

Therefore, the stored wording **“Available in most countries; some features limited in EU”** is directionally correct but incomplete. It should mention:

- Country-by-country plan availability.
- Age restrictions, including the 18+ requirement in the EEA, Switzerland, and UK for Google AI plan use.
- Feature-specific exclusions outside the EU, including Nigeria for at least some features.
- Separate availability rules for Workspace and business plans.

## 6. Official URL

**Stored data: INCORRECT or outdated if it identifies a standalone Gemini Advanced feature page.**

The current official Gemini plan page is the active Gemini web experience at:

`https://gemini.google.com/advanced`

The page currently presents **Google AI Pro and Ultra**, including Gemini 3.1 Pro, plan pricing, usage limits, and premium features.[9]

Google’s official support page for current Gemini Apps limits is also active and was updated on October 10, 2026.[1] The existence of an active current plan page and current support documentation conflicts with classifying the product as deprecated.

## 7. Recent changes in the last 30 days

**Stored data: INCOMPLETE; recent changes detected.**

Official pages show several recent changes or active updates:

- Google’s Gemini Apps limits documentation was updated **October 10, 2026**, with the current Free, AI Plus, AI Pro, and AI Ultra limit structure.[1]
- Google’s Workspace-related Gemini documentation was updated **October 10, 2026**, including current business and education availability information.[2]
- Google’s Google AI Pro help documentation was updated **October 9, 2026**.[11]
- Google’s Gemini updates page reported the rollout of **Gemini 3.1 Pro** and higher limits for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.[15]
- Google announced the **Gemini agent** at Gemini at Work 2026 on **October 8, 2026**, although that announcement concerns Google Cloud/workplace functionality rather than a direct rename of the consumer Gemini plan.[14]

The most important database changes are therefore:

1. Replace the standalone “Gemini Advanced” model with the current **Gemini Apps / Google AI plan** structure.
2. Change status from **deprecated** to **active / generally available**, with feature- and region-specific limitations.
3. Add **Google AI Plus**.
4. Replace “Full” and “Highest” with quota-based limits.
5. Mark Linux web access as available.
6. Change gating from **paid-only** to **free base access with paid upgrades**, with separate Workspace gating.
7. Retain the regional caveat but expand it to include country, age, and feature-specific restrictions.

results.response:
**The stored data is largely accurate in describing current tier benefits and platform access but uses the legacy name "Gemini Advanced," which has been superseded by Google AI subscription plans (primarily Google AI Pro as the core paid tier for advanced Gemini access).**[[1]](https://one.google.com/intl/en_us/about/google-ai-plans/)[[2]](https://one.google.com/about/articles/google-one-ai-subscription-benefits/)

Official Google One pages (one.google.com/about/google-ai-plans and related) describe the active structure as Google AI Plus (~$4.99/mo), Google AI Pro ($19.99/mo with 5 TB storage and 4x usage limits relative to free/standard), and Google AI Ultra (from ~$99.99/mo with 5x–20x Pro limits, higher storage like 20–30 TB, Deep Think reasoning, and other exclusives). These provide expanded/higher access to Gemini models (e.g., 3.1 Pro or equivalents) and features like Deep Research, with Pro/Ultra unlocking the strongest capabilities.[[1]](https://one.google.com/intl/en_us/about/google-ai-plans/)[[3]](https://one.google.com/about/google-ai-plans/?authuser=0)

"Gemini Advanced" was the prior branding for the premium Gemini experience (tied to Google One AI Premium), now integrated/rebranded under the Google AI plans. It is not prominently featured as a standalone current offering on official pricing/help pages.[[4]](https://gemini.google/advanced?hl=en)[[5]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/bard-gemini-advanced-app/)

**Key recent updates (last ~30–60 days as of Oct 12, 2026):**
- **Model access changes (effective ~Oct 9, 2026):** Free users are now limited to the Flash-Lite model only (losing Flash and Pro access). Google AI Plus subscribers lose Pro model access (retaining Flash/Flash-Lite; timing via email). Google AI Pro and Ultra retain full access to Pro models plus Deep Think (now available to Pro). This tightens the "varying access" noted for free in the stored data.[[6]](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1005451/google-gemini-free-flash-lite-only)[[7]](https://winbuzzer.com/2026/10/07/google-will-limit-free-gemini-to-one-ai-model-xcxwbn/)[[8]](https://www.igeeksblog.com/gemini-model-access-october-changes/)
- Pricing, storage, and core Pro/Ultra benefits (4x/5x–20x limits, Deep Think on higher tiers, bundled perks like storage/YouTube/Home) remain consistent with the stored data. Ultra includes exclusives like higher video generation limits and US-only features (e.g., certain agents).[[9]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/google-one/google-ai-subscriptions/)[[2]](https://one.google.com/about/articles/google-one-ai-subscription-benefits/)
- No major platform changes noted. Access remains web-based (gemini.google.com), via Gemini mobile apps (iOS/Android with system integration on Android), and API (Gemini API). Desktop is web-based; no native Linux/terminal/Chrome extensions highlighted as primary.[[1]](https://one.google.com/intl/en_us/about/google-ai-plans/)
- Regional notes: Some advanced features (e.g., Gemini Agent/Spark, certain bundles) are US-only or English-limited. Plans are available in many countries with varying pricing/offers (e.g., student deals).[[9]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/google-one/google-ai-subscriptions/)
- No explicit "deprecated" announcement for the Gemini Advanced feature/tier itself; evolution into Google AI plans is the shift. Model deprecations (separate from consumer tiers) continue on the API side.[[10]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations)

**X posts from @GoogleAI and @Google (recent, focusing on Pro/Ultra):** These confirm subscriber access to new models/features (e.g., 3.8 Flash, Omni Flash, Spark integrations) for Google AI Pro and Ultra users in the Gemini app, Search, Studio, etc., aligning with the tiered availability.[[11]](https://x.com/GoogleAI/status/2095175761783148822)[[12]](https://x.com/Google/status/2095193922884468964)

**Summary of current availability:** Matches the stored data closely—Pro as the main paid step-up for full Pro model access and 4x limits/5 TB; Ultra for highest limits/Deep Think/more storage; Free now more restricted. Platforms and API access are consistent. The main evolution is the rebranding away from "Gemini Advanced" and tighter free/Plus model restrictions in October 2026. Official sources: Google One plan pages, blog.google announcements, and Gemini help/docs. No major contradictions found.

[4][7][12] | **Incorrect:** the stored description conflates discontinued legacy add-ons with the current AI Ultra Access add-on. |

**The stored data remains largely accurate as of October 12, 2026, with minor nuances around add-on naming/evolution and bundling details.**[[1]](https://workspace.google.com/pricing?tab_activeEl=tabset-companies&hl=en_uk)[[2]](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/google-workspace-with-gemini)

Gemini in Workspace (side panel, Help me write/create, Fill with Gemini, etc., in Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Gmail, etc.) is generally available (GA). It is gated behind paid plans/subscriptions, with no evidence of deprecation or beta status changes. Core availability has been stable since the 2025 bundling into Workspace plans (no longer requiring a separate primary add-on for base features).[[3]](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/billing/ai-features-and-pricing-updates-for-google-workspace-business-editions)[[4]](https://workspace.google.com/blog/product-announcements/empowering-businesses-with-AI)

### Availability by Plan (Matches Stored Data Closely)
- **Free/personal free tier**: Very limited (basic suggestions only, if any in Workspace apps).[[5]](https://www.therundown.ai/tools/google-sheets-ai)
- **Google AI Plus** (personal): Partial/limited. Explicitly covers Gemini in Gmail, Vids, and “more,” but Docs/Sheets/Drive side-panel features like Help me create or full Fill with Gemini are **not** listed at this tier (they require Pro/Ultra).[[6]](https://9to5google.com/2026/05/25/google-ai-plus-pro-ultra-gemini-features/)[[5]](https://www.therundown.ai/tools/google-sheets-ai)
- **Google AI Pro/Ultra** (personal): Full access to Gemini in Docs, Sheets, etc. (Help me create, side panel, etc.), with higher limits on Ultra.[[6]](https://9to5google.com/2026/05/25/google-ai-plus-pro-ultra-gemini-features/)
- **Workspace plans (Business/Enterprise)**: Bundled since early 2025. Business Starter offers limited access (primarily Gmail/Vids/Gemini app). Business Standard/Plus and Enterprise editions provide full Gemini in Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Meet, Chat, etc. (side panel, Help me write/create, etc.).[[1]](https://workspace.google.com/pricing?tab_activeEl=tabset-companies&hl=en_uk)[[1]](https://workspace.google.com/pricing?tab_activeEl=tabset-companies&hl=en_uk)
- **Workspace add-on**: Full/advanced access via supplements like **AI Expanded Access** (higher limits, advanced image/video generation, deep research, etc.). The prior **AI Ultra Access** add-on (or Google AI Ultra for Business) has been phased out/transitioned (removals starting ~July 2026, with automatic shifts to Expanded Access). This aligns with the stored note on the add-on for advanced features.[[7]](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/ai-ultra-access)

No major pricing or tier-restriction announcements in the last 30–60 days. The structure has been consistent post-2025 changes.[[8]](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/welcome-to-gemini-at-work-2026)

### Platforms
- **Web**: Full support in Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Gmail, etc. (primary access method).[[2]](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/google-workspace-with-gemini)
- **Mobile (iOS/Android)**: Supported via Workspace mobile apps.
- **Windows/macOS**: Web apps (no native desktop app changes noted).
- **Linux, Chrome extension, terminal**: No support indicated (matches stored data).
- **API**: Available via Gemini API (separate from in-app Workspace features).

No platform availability updates in recent official sources.

### Other Notes
- **Regional/rollout**: Features are widely available with language support (25+ languages for side panels); no new country restrictions or major rollouts noted recently.
- **Recent enhancements (not availability changes)**: Side-panel feature parity/upgrades across apps (e.g., cross-app tasks) rolled out around September 2026 for eligible plans. Newer capabilities like advanced “Help me create” and spreadsheet building have been available to Pro/Ultra and qualifying Workspace users since earlier in 2026.[[9]](https://9to5google.com/2026/09/09/gemini-workspace-side-panel-upgrade/)
- **X (@GoogleAI, @Google)**: Recent/official posts focus on model capabilities, benchmarks (e.g., Sheets performance), and integrations rather than pricing, tier shifts, or platform changes. No contradictions to stored data.[[10]](https://x.com/GoogleAI/status/2095175761783148822)

**Official sources cited** (pricing/help/docs pages): workspace.google.com/pricing, knowledge.workspace.google.com (e.g., Google Workspace with Gemini pages and AI features/pricing updates), and related support articles. No conflicting information from verified accounts or recent announcements. The data is up-to-date with only the noted add-on evolution (Ultra Access → Expanded Access).

As of **October 12, 2026, the stored record is no longer accurate**: Google has announced that **Gems are being replaced by “Skills” and support for Gems will be removed on a phased schedule**. Existing Gems are intended to be migrated automatically to Skills.[1]

## 1. Pricing-tier availability and limits — **INCORRECT**

Google’s current information indicates:

| Plan | Gemini Apps usage limit | Gems status |
|---|---:|---|
| Free / no AI plan | Standard limits | Gems are being transitioned to Skills |
| Google AI Plus | 2× standard | Gems are being transitioned to Skills |
| Google AI Pro | 4× standard | Gems are being transitioned to Skills |
| Google AI Ultra | 5× or 20× Pro, depending on subscription | Gems are being transitioned to Skills |
| Workspace add-on | Depends on the eligible Workspace edition/add-on | Workspace Gems support is scheduled for later removal |

Google describes these as **Gemini Apps’ overall compute-based limits**, not necessarily limits specific to creating or running Gems. Limits depend on factors such as the model, feature, prompt complexity, and conversation length; the limits refresh every five hours until the applicable weekly limit is reached.[3]

The stored record is therefore incorrect in two ways:

- **Google AI Pro is listed as “Full,”** but Google’s current Gemini Apps limits page describes Pro as **4× standard limits**, not unlimited/full access.[3]
- **“Gems” should no longer be treated as a stable GA feature.** Google announced that Skills will assume the relevant Gems functionality and that Gems support will be removed.[1]

Google’s subscription pages list Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra as the paid consumer AI plans.[9][10] The Workspace route is separate: Workspace users require an eligible Workspace edition or an applicable AI add-on, and feature availability varies by edition.[2][4]

## 2. Platform and surface availability — **INCORRECT / NEEDS REVISION**

The stored platform matrix is not fully verifiable from the gathered official material, and the transition to Skills makes the original “Gems” matrix outdated.

| Surface | Current assessment |
|---|---|
| Windows | **Available through the web app**, rather than as a distinct native Windows Gems client |
| macOS | **Available through the web app**, rather than as a distinct native macOS Gems client |
| Linux | **Available through the web app** if the supported web experience is accessible; the stored ❌ is not justified as a product-level restriction |
| iOS | **Available through Gemini’s supported mobile experience**, subject to account, region, and rollout conditions |
| Android | **Available through Gemini’s supported mobile experience**, subject to account, region, and rollout conditions |
| Web | **Available** |
| Terminal | **No official Gemini Apps Gems surface established** |
| API | **Not equivalent to Gemini Apps Gems**; Gemini API custom-agent functionality should not be counted as the consumer Gems feature |

The stored entries for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and web appear to describe access to Gemini generally rather than a separately documented Gems implementation. The **Linux ❌ is especially unreliable**, because browser-based access is not inherently limited by operating system. Conversely, the stored **API ✅** should be removed unless the database intentionally treats separate Gemini API agent functionality as equivalent to Gems.

Because Google is transitioning the feature to Skills, the correct record should distinguish:

- **Gemini Apps / web and mobile surfaces**
- **Workspace surfaces**
- **Gemini API capabilities**

They should not be represented as one identical “Gems” feature.

## 3. Current status — **INCORRECT**

The stored status `ga` is no longer accurate for Gems.

Google announced on **September 30, 2026** that Skills will replace Gems and that support for Gems will be removed in stages.[1] The relevant status is therefore:

> **Deprecated / sunset announced; migration to Skills in progress**

The announced schedule is:

- **November 2026:** removal for individuals using personal accounts
- **March 2027:** removal for Workspace Business, Enterprise, and nonprofit customers
- **June 2027:** removal for Workspace Education customers[1][5]

Google says existing Gems will be **automatically migrated into Skills** when Gems are removed.[1]

## 4. Access gating — **INCORRECT**

The stored value `free` is too broad.

Historically, Google made Gems available to users without a paid AI plan, and current Gemini Apps documentation still distinguishes **standard limits without an AI plan** from higher paid-plan limits.[3] However, availability is not simply “free” across all account types and surfaces:

- Personal-account access is subject to Gemini Apps availability and applicable regional/account restrictions.
- Paid Google AI plans provide higher Gemini usage limits.[3]
- Workspace access depends on an eligible Workspace edition or add-on.[2][4]
- Some Workspace AI capabilities require an administrator-enabled entitlement or add-on.[15]

A more accurate gating value would be:

> **Free with standard Gemini Apps access; higher limits paid; Workspace access org/plan dependent; feature deprecated**

Thus the stored `free` value is **INCORRECT as a complete classification**, although it correctly captures that a paid consumer subscription was not universally required.

## 5. Regional availability — **INCORRECT / UNSUPPORTED**

The stored note **“Available globally” cannot be confirmed** from the gathered official sources and should not remain as an unconditional statement.

Google’s documentation indicates that Gemini and Google AI plan availability varies by:

- Country or territory
- Account type
- Age eligibility
- Workspace edition
- Product rollout and local availability

Google’s announcement also says the new Skills experience is currently available to users **18 and older**, with support for users under 18 planned later.[1]

Recommended regional value:

> **Available in supported Gemini countries and territories; not guaranteed globally. Availability and limits vary by country, account type, age, and Workspace edition.**

The record should also note the U18 limitation reported in Google’s announcement.[1]

## 6. Official URL — **UPDATED**

The current official announcement and migration information is:

- **Google Blog: “Let skills in Gemini tackle your most repetitive tasks”**[1]

Google’s official Gemini Apps limits documentation is:

- **Gemini Apps limits & upgrades for Google AI subscribers**[3]

The official product page for the consumer AI plans is Google One’s Google AI plans page.[9][10]

The prior Gems-specific URL, if present in the database, should be replaced or supplemented with the Skills announcement because Google has announced the feature’s retirement and migration.

## 7. Recent changes in the last 30 days — **CHANGE DETECTED**

A significant change occurred within the requested 30-day period:

- On **September 30, 2026**, Google announced **Skills**, a successor to Gems.[1]
- Google stated that Skills will include key Gems capabilities, including sharing and adding files from Google Drive and notebooks from Gemini Notebook.[1]
- Google announced the phased removal of Gems beginning in **November 2026** for personal accounts, followed by Workspace customer groups in 2027.[1][5]
- Google’s limits documentation was updated in October 2026 and currently lists standard, 2×, 4×, and Ultra higher-limit tiers for Gemini Apps.[3]

### Recommended corrected record

```json
{
  "name": "Gems / Skills (transition)",
  "category": "agents",
  "status": "deprecated",
  "gating": "free with standard Gemini access; paid higher limits; Workspace plan dependent",
  "availability": {
    "free": "Available during transition, standard Gemini limits",
    "google_ai_plus": "Available during transition, 2x standard Gemini limits",
    "google_ai_pro": "Available during transition, 4x standard Gemini limits",
    "google_ai_ultra": "Available during transition, 5x or 20x Pro limits depending on subscription",
    "workspace_add_on": "Availability depends on eligible Workspace edition/add-on"
  },
  "regional_availability": "Supported countries and territories; not guaranteed globally",
  "migration": "Gems are being replaced by Skills; automatic migration announced",
  "sunset": {
    "personal_accounts": "November 2026",
    "workspace_business_enterprise_nonprofit": "March 2027",
    "workspace_education": "June 2027"
  }
}
```

Overall, the stored record requires updates to **status, gating, regional wording, Pro limits, API classification, and the feature name/official URL**.

**The stored data is largely accurate for the pre-transition state of Gemini Gems (free access across tiers with tiered usage limits, broad platform support excluding Linux/Chrome/terminal, GA status, and API availability), but it is now outdated due to a major announced transition.**[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)

Google officially announced on September 30, 2026, that **Skills** (a more modular, reusable system for custom instructions, invocable via “/” commands, with support for reference files) will replace Gems. Skills are rolling out globally in the Gemini chat app (starting around October 13, 2026, for the app; earlier in Workspace), while Gems support is being phased out.[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)

### Key Recent Changes (Last ~30–60 Days, as of Oct 12, 2026)
- **Deprecation/Transition (Status Change)**: Gems are moving from active GA to phased replacement by Skills. Automatic migration of existing Gems to Skills is planned. Timeline for personal accounts: Gems move to Settings panel on/around November 17, 2026 (still usable until migrated); full removal of support starts in November 2026. Workspace business/enterprise/nonprofit: no sooner than March 2027. Education: no sooner than June 2027. Opal (related experiment) is also sunsetting.[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)[[2]](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/generative-ai/gemini-app/about-the-transition-to-skills)[[3]](https://www.androidauthority.com/gemini-gems-phase-out-timeline-3717503/)
- **Pricing/Tiers/Availability**: No fundamental changes to the free gating or tier structure (Free with standard limits; Google AI Plus with ~2x limits; Pro with higher limits/sharing; Ultra with highest limits). Gems/Skills remain available without a paid subscription for personal accounts (usage limits scale with plan). Recent sources confirm the tier ladder and that the feature itself is not paywalled.[[4]](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/gemini-skills)[[5]](https://aitoolanalysis.com/gemini-gems-review/)[[6]](https://costbench.com/software/ai-chatbots/gemini/)
- **Platforms**: No updates contradicting the stored data. Gems have been available on web (gemini.google.com), iOS/Android apps, and desktop (Windows/macOS via web or apps); creation often easiest on web. API access exists via Gemini API for related custom behaviors. No mentions of Linux, standalone Chrome extension, or terminal support.[[7]](https://www.zdnet.com/article/gemini-gems-are-now-available-for-free-users-and-on-android-and-ios/)
- **Other**: No new regional restrictions or rollouts noted in official sources. Skills aim to add/enhance features like sharing and Drive integration that Gems had.[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)

**Official sources cited**:
- Google Blog post (Sep 30, 2026): “Automate repetitive tasks with Skills” (primary announcement on replacement and timeline).[[1]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/automate-tasks-with-skills/)
- Related coverage and help references in the announcement (e.g., transition help center links).
- Supporting context from Google Workspace help/docs and pricing/subscription pages referenced in secondary reporting.

In summary, Gems remain functional with the described availability as of mid-October 2026, but users should prepare for the Skills transition starting in November (personal accounts). The stored data should be updated to reflect the deprecation and replacement by Skills for accuracy going forward.

### Key Changes (Primarily from August–October 2026)
- **Feature status**: Imagen models (e.g., `imagen-4.0-generate-001`, `imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-001`, `imagen-4.0-fast-generate-001`, and earlier versions) reached end-of-life. Shutdown occurred as early as August 17, 2026 (Gemini API deprecations table lists this date; some surfaces had earlier migration deadlines). Official documentation now states: “Imagen is shut down and no longer available through the Gemini API. Use Nano Banana for image generation and editing.”[[3]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations)[[4]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog)
- **Replacement**: Google has migrated users to native Gemini image generation models, branded internally/recently as “Nano Banana” (e.g., `gemini-3.1-flash-image` / Nano Banana 2, now updated to `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` GA on October 6, 2026; also `gemini-3-pro-image` / Nano Banana Pro and lighter variants). These are the current GA image-gen offerings.[[4]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog)[[5]](https://releaseterminal.app/events/gemini-nano-banana-2-1-is-generally-available-in-the-gemini/)
- **Pricing/tiers and gating**: The stored plan-specific limits (~10-20/day Free, 2x Free for Plus, ~100-150/day Pro, 5x–20x Pro for Ultra) and “Imagen 4 access” notes no longer apply to Imagen. Current image generation (Nano Banana models) uses token-based or per-image pricing in the Gemini API (e.g., output image pricing around $0.03–$0.06+ per image depending on variant/resolution, with batch discounts; free tier availability varies by surface like AI Studio). Subscription benefits (Google AI Pro/Ultra) provide higher rate limits or access in consumer apps, but details are now tied to Gemini models rather than Imagen.[[6]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing)[[7]](https://notifications.google.com/g/p/ANiao5ohvCzVa8wFXu2St2a0NNaIPI6PM-QKasyMOEVlvwl8TmMvd4avqcOGtWXR3vCAcNyZ7iOjqbkcm7-bEoQwCQ5NHOznrgQFYuh63_KZWHtDFXMmGnvD8LhQmwloi12uXcpp4bHZGPgB1Vg)

No evidence of changes restoring Imagen on Linux, Chrome, or terminal; API access has shifted to the new models. Consumer app/web/mobile availability for image gen persists under the Gemini branding.[[2]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/image-generation)
- **Regional/ other notes**: No specific new regional rollouts or restrictions for Imagen were found (as it is shut down). Recent announcements focus on Nano Banana 2.1 GA, deprecations, and migrations.[[4]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog)

- Gemini API pricing: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing (updated ~Oct 9, 2026).[[6]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing)
- Gemini deprecations: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations (lists Imagen shutdown dates and Nano Banana replacements).[[3]](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations)

**The stored data remains largely accurate as of October 2026, with minor clarifications from official sources.** Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro Image) launched on November 20, 2025, as a higher-fidelity image generation/editing model built on Gemini 3 Pro. It offers improved text rendering, world knowledge/reasoning, consistency (up to 5 people/14 images), editing controls, and resolutions up to 4K.[[1]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/nano-banana-pro/)[[2]](https://blog.google/products/gemini/where-to-use-nano-banana-pro/)

### Pricing/Tier Availability (No Major Recent Changes)
- **Free plan**: Limited quotas in the Gemini app (reverts to the base Nano Banana model afterward). Google’s $0 plan references limited access via Google Flow.[[1]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/nano-banana-pro/)[[2]](https://blog.google/products/gemini/where-to-use-nano-banana-pro/)
- **Google AI Plus**: Higher quotas than Free (as part of “Everything in Free…”), but full/unrestricted Nano Banana Pro access starts at the Pro tier.[[1]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/nano-banana-pro/)
- **Google AI Pro**: Full access (e.g., via three-dot menu in the app for specialized/Pro tasks).[[3]](https://www.theverge.com/tech/885275/google-nano-banana-2-ai-image-model-gemini-launch)
- **Google AI Ultra**: Highest limits (everything in Pro + more).[[1]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/nano-banana-pro/)

A February 26, 2026 update introduced **Nano Banana 2** (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image) as the new default/fast option across modes in the Gemini app and other surfaces. Pro remains available for higher-tier subscribers (Pro/Ultra) via the three-dot menu for specialized/high-fidelity tasks. No pricing or tier changes noted in the last 30–60 days.[[3]](https://www.theverge.com/tech/885275/google-nano-banana-2-ai-image-model-gemini-launch)[[4]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/nano-banana-2/)

API access exists via the Gemini API (model ID references like gemini-3-pro-image or preview variants), with per-image pricing (separate from consumer plans).[[5]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/gemini-3-pro-image-developers/)

### Platform Availability
- **Web (gemini.google.com)** and desktop web: ✅ (web-based).
- **iOS/Android Gemini app**: ✅ (primary consumer access; globally available).
- **Windows/macOS**: ✅ (via web).
- **Linux, dedicated Chrome extension, terminal**: ❌ (no mentions in official docs).
- **API**: ✅ (Gemini API / Google AI Studio / Vertex AI for developers/enterprise).[[2]](https://blog.google/products/gemini/where-to-use-nano-banana-pro/)[[6]](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/nano-banana-pro-available-for-enterprise)

It is also rolling out/available in NotebookLM, Google Workspace tools (Slides, Vids), AI Mode in Search (with some regional notes, e.g., U.S./English initially for certain tiers), and enterprise options.[[2]](https://blog.google/products/gemini/where-to-use-nano-banana-pro/)[[7]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/where-to-use-nano-banana-pro/)

### Status and Other Updates
- **Status**: Launched in preview/rolling rollout in Nov 2025; made generally available (GA) by mid-2026 (confirmed in official @Google and @GoogleAI posts around May–June 2026). No deprecation noted.[[8]](https://x.com/GoogleAI/status/2062942864288387430)[[9]](https://x.com/Google/status/2060029132105191723)
- **Regional**: Global rollout in the Gemini app; some surfaces (e.g., AI Mode in Search) had initial geographic/language limits. No new country restrictions or major rollouts reported recently.[[7]](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/where-to-use-nano-banana-pro/)
- **Recent changes (last 30–60 days)**: None identified in official announcements or verified @Google/@GoogleAI posts. The main evolution was the earlier Nano Banana 2 default shift (Feb 2026), after which Pro access stabilized for paid tiers.[[4]](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/ai/nano-banana-2/)

**Official sources cited**: Google Blog posts (e.g., “Nano Banana Pro: Gemini 3 Pro Image model,” “Where to use Google’s image generator Nano Banana Pro now,” developer/Workspace updates from Nov–Dec 2025 and Feb 2026); X posts from @Google and @GoogleAI (GA announcements, May–June 2026). No contradictory information found on pricing, platforms, or status. The stored data aligns closely with these details.

results.response:
As of **October 12, 2026**, the stored record is **partly correct but needs updates**. The main changes are that Google now describes the allowance as **AI Credits** rather than only “Flow credits,” AI Plus is explicitly supported, Ultra provides **25,000 monthly credits**, and current official pages distinguish access in the Gemini app from access through Flow.

## 1. Pricing-tier availability

| Plan | Current finding | Comparison with stored data |
|---|---|---|
| **Free** | No general access to full Veo video generation is documented. Some users may receive limited access to **Veo 3.1 Lite** trials or lower-priority experiences, depending on the product and region. | **INCORRECT / needs qualification**: “Not available” is too absolute. |
| **Google AI Plus** | Includes Gemini video-generation access and **200 monthly AI Credits** for Flow. | **CORRECT**, although “AI Credits” is the current terminology. |
| **Google AI Pro** | Includes Veo access in Gemini and full Flow access, with **1,000 monthly AI Credits**. | **CORRECT**. |
| **Google AI Ultra** | Includes the highest Veo access and **25,000 monthly AI Credits**. | **INCORRECT**: the stored “10,000–25,000” range should be replaced with the current listed allowance of 25,000. |
| **Workspace add-on** | Workspace users can access Veo 3.1 in Google Vids with the applicable AI Ultra Access or Workspace licensing; this is not equivalent to consumer Gemini-plan access. | **PARTLY CORRECT**: “limited” is too vague and the entitlement depends on the Workspace license. |

Google states that AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra provide 200, 1,000, and 25,000 monthly credits, respectively.[1][4] Google’s Flow documentation also lists different per-generation costs: Veo 3.1 Fast costs 20 credits for non-Ultra subscribers and 10 for Ultra subscribers, while Veo 3.1 Quality costs 100 credits for all users.[1] Credits refresh each billing cycle and unused credits do not roll over.[1][4]

**Exact change to stored data:**  
- Change **“Flow credits”** to **“AI Credits usable in Flow”** where applicable.  
- Change Ultra from **“10,000–25,000”** to **“25,000 monthly AI Credits.”**  
- Qualify the Free tier because limited Veo 3.1 Lite access or trials may exist even though full paid-tier Veo access is not included.  
- Treat Workspace access as a separate organization-managed entitlement.

## 2. Platform and surface availability

| Surface | Current finding | Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** | Available through supported web browsers, including Gemini and Flow. | **CORRECT** |
| **macOS** | Available through the web. | **CORRECT** |
| **Linux** | Available through the web where the browser and region are supported. | **CORRECT** |
| **iOS** | Gemini app and related Google surfaces are supported, subject to app version, account, and regional rollout. | **CORRECT** |
| **Android** | Gemini and Flow support is documented. | **CORRECT** |
| **Web** | Available through Gemini and Flow. | **CORRECT** |
| **Terminal** | No official end-user terminal interface is documented. | **CORRECT** |
| **API** | Veo is available through Google’s developer platforms, including the Gemini API/AI Studio and Vertex AI, subject to model, project, billing, and regional availability. | **CORRECT**, but model availability should be checked separately from the consumer Gemini entitlement. |

Google’s Flow help pages document access through computer and mobile surfaces and require a qualifying Google AI subscription for Flow.[7][9] The Gemini Veo page and Google AI plan pages identify Veo as part of the Gemini experience.[6][11]

**Stored platform data: CORRECT, with one qualification:** web access is browser-based rather than a native Windows, macOS, or Linux application. “API” should not be interpreted as automatically included with a consumer subscription; API access is separately governed by developer-platform eligibility and billing.

## 3. Current status

**Stored status: CORRECT — GA.**

Veo is presented as an active production feature in Gemini, Flow, Google AI plan benefits, and Workspace offerings. Current documentation refers to Veo 3.1 and its production usage limits rather than labeling the overall feature deprecated or invite-only.[1][6][11]

Some individual models or capabilities may be experimental or lower-priority—for example, Veo 3.1 Lite—but that does not change the general availability status of Veo video generation.

## 4. Access gating

**Stored gating: PARTLY CORRECT.**

The feature is **paid-gated for full, standard access**: Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra is required for the relevant subscription experiences, and Flow requires one of those plans.[7][9] However, the current documentation indicates limited trials or Lite access may be available to some users without the same full paid entitlement.[11]

The more precise classification is:

- **Full consumer access:** paid subscription.
- **Limited trial/Lite access:** may be available to eligible users, depending on region and rollout.
- **Workspace access:** organization-managed or license-managed.
- **API access:** separately gated by developer account, project, model availability, and billing.

Therefore, replace the simple value **“paid”** with **“paid for full access; limited trial/Lite access may be available; Workspace/API access separately gated.”**

## 5. Regional availability

**Stored regional statement: PARTLY CORRECT.**

Veo is not globally uniform. Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra are offered only in supported countries and territories; Google’s Gemini Veo page states that the plans are available in more than 140 countries and territories, while AI Plus is available in more than 160 countries.[6] Availability therefore depends on both the country and the specific plan.

The stored restriction concerning **image-to-video/photo-to-video in the EEA, United Kingdom, and Switzerland** should be retained where it applies to the relevant Gemini feature. It should not be generalized to mean that all Veo text-to-video generation is unavailable in those regions.

Additional country-specific constraints can affect:

- Whether Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra can be purchased.
- Whether Flow is available.
- Which Veo model is offered.
- Whether image-to-video or other input modes are enabled.
- Workspace licensing and administrator controls.
- API model availability and regional endpoint eligibility.
- Top-up-credit availability; Google’s Ultra documentation specifically notes an exception for top-up credits in Japan.[15]

**Recommended regional wording:**  
“Available in countries and territories where the relevant Gemini, Flow, Workspace, or API offering is supported. Plan and model availability varies by country. Image-to-video/photo-to-video may be restricted in the EEA, UK, and Switzerland; additional country-specific limitations apply.”

## 6. Official URL

The official Gemini Veo page is:

**https://gemini.google.com/veo**

It remains active and displays current Veo and Google AI plan information.[6]

Other official supporting pages include Google’s Flow credit documentation, which is the more authoritative source for current credit allowances and generation costs.[1] The Gemini subscription pages also remain active for plan-specific benefits.[11][14][15]

**Overall**: The stored data accurately reflects current paid-tier gating, credit allocations, platform support, and GA status. **The stored data remains accurate as of October 12, 2026, with no major changes to pricing/tiers, core platform availability, feature status (still GA), or regional restrictions in the last 30-60 days.**[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)

Official Microsoft Learn documentation (updated as recently as September 30, 2026) confirms Agent Builder as a generally available (GA) no-code tool for building declarative agents inside Microsoft 365 Copilot. It is integrated into the M365 Copilot experience for quick, natural-language or manual configuration of agents grounded in organizational data (e.g., SharePoint, Microsoft Graph).[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[2]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder-build-agents)

### Licensing and Availability (Pricing/Tiers)
- **Requires Microsoft 365 Copilot** (the paid add-on, typically ~$30/user/month) for full authoring and advanced capabilities like tenant data grounding.[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[3]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-studio-experience)
- Basic agents (web/public knowledge only) can be built/used via Copilot Chat without the full Copilot license in some cases, aligning with the “limited”/⚠️ note for Copilot Chat (M365 commercial).[[3]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-studio-experience)[[3]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-studio-experience)
- Not available for consumer plans (Free, Personal/Family, or M365 Premium/consumer), which may include prebuilt agents but not authoring.[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)
- More advanced/multi-step or external-publishing agents move to Copilot Studio (separate licensing/credits model with pay-as-you-go or packs).[[3]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-studio-experience)[[4]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/copilot-studio)
- No announcements of new paid tiers, price changes, or expanded free access in recent official sources. Minor capability updates (e.g., default features for new agents) rolled out globally in late August 2026 with no impact on licensing.[[5]](https://m365admin.handsontek.net/agent-builder-capabilities-update/)

### Platforms
- **Supported**: Web (microsoft365.com/chat, office.com/chat), Microsoft Teams desktop and web clients, and M365 Copilot app toolbar (Work/Web options). Windows and macOS via these apps/clients.[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)
- **Not supported**: Mobile apps (explicitly stated as unavailable on mobile versions), Linux, standalone Chrome/terminal, or direct API authoring (advanced actions/integrations route through Copilot Studio).[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)
- No updates to platform support in the reviewed period.

### Feature Status and Other Notes
- **GA status** is consistent across current docs; it is positioned as the lightweight, in-context option versus Copilot Studio for complex needs. Skills/custom actions remain in preview (Frontier Program only).[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[3]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-studio-experience)
- **Regional**: Available in a broad list of countries/regions (via Power Platform default environment) plus GCC/GCCH (with admin notes on sharing in GCCH). No new rollouts or restrictions noted recently.[[6]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder-regional-availability)
- Recent minor updates (April and August 2026) focused on improved creation experience, knowledge setup, and default capabilities—no deprecation or breaking changes.[[5]](https://m365admin.handsontek.net/agent-builder-capabilities-update/)[[7]](https://m365admin.handsontek.net/agent-builder-microsoft-365-copilot-updates-agent-creation-experience/)
- No relevant recent posts found from official X accounts (@MSFTCopilot or Microsoft) matching searches for “Agent Builder” since August 2026.

**Sources cited**: Primary official pages include the Agent Builder overview and build guides on Microsoft Learn (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder and related articles, updated Sept 2026), Copilot Studio comparison and licensing docs, and supporting Microsoft Copilot Blog/pricing pages.[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[3]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/copilot-studio-experience)[[1]](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/agent-builder)[[4]](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/pricing/copilot-studio)

The stored data aligns closely with these sources. Minor nuances (e.g., exact regional lists or Frontier preview details) exist but do not contradict the summary.

**The stored data is mostly accurate in plan/platform availability and limits but outdated in key nomenclature, feature positioning, and some details due to the July 2026 launch of GPT-Live.**[[1]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)

OpenAI introduced **GPT-Live** (GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini) on July 8, 2026, as a new full-duplex (continuous listen-and-speak) voice system. It became the default for ChatGPT Voice globally on iOS, Android, and web (chatgpt.com), replacing Advanced Voice Mode as the primary experience.[[1]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/)[[1]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/)

### Key Updates from Official Sources
- **"Live" (GPT-Live-1 / mini) is now the main/default mode**: It offers more natural conversations, better turn-taking/interruptions, background delegation to frontier models (e.g., GPT-5.5), web search/memory/widgets, and visual results. It does *not* support video or screen sharing.[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)
- **Advanced Voice Mode is now legacy/previous real-time experience**: It remains available (especially on mobile) specifically for video and screen sharing capabilities. Standard (turn-based) is also still an option.[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)
- **Plan availability and limits** (Voice in Chat, rolling 24-hour): Aligns closely with stored data. Free gets limited GPT-Live-1 mini; Go/Plus get ~3 hours GPT-Live-1 (or mini); higher Pro tiers get more/unlimited; Business/Enterprise have caps or credit-based/custom (e.g., 1.25 credits/min or $0.05/min). Desktop voice has separate pricing/limits.[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)
- **Platforms**: 
  - Web (chatgpt.com with mic): Yes.
  - iOS/Android: Full support (best on mobile for some legacy features).
  - Desktop apps (macOS/Windows): Available on paid plans (Voice in Desktop for tasks/agents); macOS support aligns with the July 2026 timeline ("returned").
  - Linux, Chrome extension, terminal: No mentions of support.
  - API: GPT-Live-1 available (launched ~Sep 10, 2026) for developers.[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live-1-in-the-api/)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)
- **Business/Enterprise**: Available subject to workspace settings; admin controls apply for Enterprise. Voice in Chat (web/mobile) and Desktop supported.[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)
- **Other**: Global rollout (no new regional restrictions announced). No deprecation of the overall voice feature. Legacy Advanced/Standard remain accessible where needed.[[1]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/)

### Recent Changes (Last 30-60 Days as of Oct 12, 2026)
The major shift was the July 8, 2026 GPT-Live launch (with follow-on API availability in September). Help Center pages reflect ongoing updates (e.g., limits, desktop details, legacy options). No major new pricing changes, tier restrictions, or platform rollouts noted in the most recent official docs or @OpenAI posts in the results.[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001274)[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live-1-in-the-api/)

**Sources cited**: Primary official pages include the GPT-Live announcement (openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-live/), ChatGPT Voice Help Center (help.openai.com/articles/20001274), and related API/docs pages. X searches from @OpenAI yielded older posts on prior Advanced Voice updates (pre-2026). No conflicting recent announcements found.

No major deprecations, status changes, or broad regional restrictions were announced in the last 30–60 days.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9793128-about-chatgpt-pro-tiers)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes)

### Key Findings from Official Sources
- **Pricing/Plans and Model Availability**: Plans align closely with the stored data (Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise). Free/Go use lighter models with rate limits; higher tiers offer more access. Recent transitions include GPT-6 models rolling out in the Chat tab: GPT-6 Sol for Plus/Pro/Business/Enterprise (starting ~Oct 7, 2026) and GPT-6 Luna for Free/Go (starting ~Oct 8). This matches the stored notes on transitions/rollouts around September 2026, with ongoing or completed shifts from GPT-5.5 variants. Pro now includes more granular tiers (e.g., Pro 100/200/500, with Pro 500 adding Ultrafast access for GPT-6 Astra and similar). Business/Enterprise retain Plus-like features plus admin/SSO/security options. API access uses models like GPT-5.4 variants, GPT-6 Astra, etc., with 1M+ context options noted in rate cards.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9793128-about-chatgpt-pro-tiers)[[3]](https://help.openai.com/articles/20001415)[[4]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2107895006350791071)[[5]](https://openai.com/index/gpt-6-for-everyone/)
