Official desktop apps exist for Windows (Microsoft Store) and macOS (unified app combining Chat/Work/Codex). iOS/Android apps are available. Web access is at chatgpt.com. No official Chrome extension or terminal app. Linux now has a desktop app in public preview (Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 LTS, Debian 13, Fedora 43/44), updating the stored "❌" status.[[6]](https://help.openai.com/articles/9275200-downloading-the-chatgpt-macos-app)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes)[[7]](https://help.openai.com/articles/9982051-using-the-chatgpt-windows-app)

Other notes (e.g., model retirements like o3 in some contexts) do not affect the core Chat feature.[[8]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9022015-im-travelling-to-a-different-country-and-i-cant-access-chatgpt-or-the-api)[[9]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5347006-openai-api-supported-countries-and-territories)[[10]](https://community.openai.com/t/gpt-6-is-now-rolling-out-to-all-chatgpt-users/1404163)

- **Gating and plans**: Available on Free/Go (limited usage), Plus (included with standard access), Pro (higher limits/priority compute; new Pro 500 tier introduced ~Sept 29, 2026, for highest limits + Ultrafast mode), Business, and Enterprise (custom/higher limits, admin controls). Edu is also supported in multiple references. Free/Go access appears ongoing (with caps), consistent with the stored “free” gating and limited notes. Recent model rollouts (e.g., GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol/Luna) are available to these paid tiers in Codex.[[1]](https://developers.openai.com/codex)[[2]](https://openai.com/codex/)[[4]](https://theaiagentindex.com/agents/openai-codex)[[5]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2104993967985381673)

  - Web: Yes (chatgpt.com/codex or openai.com/codex; Codex cloud/web access).[[2]](https://openai.com/codex/)
  - Terminal/CLI: Yes (`npm i -g @openai/codex`).[[2]](https://openai.com/codex/)
  - Desktop: Windows and macOS apps (full support noted; Linux primarily CLI-focused).[[2]](https://openai.com/codex/)[[6]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-codex-app/)
  - Mobile: Limited/iOS support referenced; Android less explicitly detailed but aligns with “limited” notes.[[4]](https://theaiagentindex.com/agents/openai-codex)

**No, the stored data is no longer accurate.** OpenAI has announced plans to retire custom GPTs (with migration to plugins), and new creation/publishing is now restricted on personal plans.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554407)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554397)

Key updates from official OpenAI Help Center pages (primarily https://help.openai.com/articles/8554407, https://help.openai.com/articles/8554397, and related GPTs/Enterprise articles, updated as recently as ~21 hours ago as of the search):

- **Feature status and creation restrictions**: Custom GPTs are being retired (Enterprise workspaces targeted for Dec 11, 2026; other plans expected to follow similar timelines with in-product notices). New GPT creation and publishing are **not available** on personal ChatGPT accounts (Free, Go, Plus, Pro). Existing GPTs remain usable (and editable where plan/permissions allow) until retirement. Business, Enterprise, and Edu workspaces can still create, edit, and publish GPTs subject to workspace settings and permissions.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554407)[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554397)[[1]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554407)
- **"Actions" and related capabilities**: GPTs can include apps or actions (but not both). The feature is transitioning; custom actions do not transfer in the planned migration to plugins.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554407)
- **Plan availability (creation vs. use)**: 
  - Free/Go/Plus/Pro: Use public/shared GPTs only (no new creation/publishing). Editing of existing ones may still be possible under prior eligibility.
  - Business/Enterprise/Edu: Creation, editing, sharing, and publishing remain available per workspace settings/permissions (private/team GPTs supported).[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554397)[[3]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8798620-gpts-chatgpt-team-version)
- **Platforms**: GPT creation and editing are available on the **web** (chatgpt.com). Mobile apps support **using** GPTs but **not creating** them. No specific updates noted for desktop apps (Windows/macOS), Linux, Chrome extension, terminal, or direct API (this remains a ChatGPT product feature, not an API one).[[2]](https://help.openai.com/articles/8554397)
- **Other notes**: No recent changes mentioned to regional availability. Pricing pages (openai.com/pricing and chatgpt/pricing) reference custom GPTs in higher-tier descriptions (e.g., Plus/Pro/Business) but do not override the Help Center restrictions on new creation.[[4]](https://openai.com/pricing)[[5]](https://openai.com/chatgpt/pricing)

**Recent changes (last 30-60 days, as of Oct 12, 2026)**: The retirement announcement and migration guidance (targeted migration experience around mid-September 2026) appear to be the primary recent development, with Help Center pages reflecting the shift away from new custom GPT creation on personal plans. No contradictory official X posts from @OpenAI were found in recent searches.[[6]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11391654-chatgpt-business-release-notes)

In summary, the feature has moved from broad GA (with paid gating for creation) to a deprecation phase with significant restrictions on personal plans and an upcoming full retirement. Business/Enterprise workspaces retain more flexibility. Always check the latest in-product notices or Help Center for account-specific timelines.

As of **October 12, 2026**, the stored record is **partly incorrect**. OpenAI has retired the official DALL·E experience in ChatGPT and replaced it with **ChatGPT Images**; however, image generation remains available across all ChatGPT subscription tiers. DALL·E models were also removed from the API on May 12, 2026.[1][3][5]

## 1. Pricing-tier availability and limits

**Stored data: INCORRECT.**

| Plan | Current availability | Current limits / notes |
|---|---|---|
| Free | **Available** | Subject to separate image-generation limits; OpenAI does not publish a fixed “~2/day” limit in the cited current documentation. |
| Go | **Available** | Subject to separate image-generation limits; the cited documentation does not substantiate “10× free.” |
| Plus | **Available** | Subject to separate image-generation limits. |
| Pro | **Available** | Subject to separate image-generation limits; “unlimited” is not substantiated as an unconditional guarantee. |
| Business | **Available** | ChatGPT Images is available; “Images with thinking” is also available on Business.[1] |
| Enterprise | **Available for ChatGPT Images** | “Images with thinking” was still listed as coming soon for Enterprise, so the two capabilities should not be conflated.[1] |

OpenAI states that **ChatGPT Images is available on all tiers**.[1] Image generation has separate limits from ordinary chat, uploads, voice, and other tools, but the current public documentation does not provide the fixed per-plan quantities recorded in the database.[9][15]

The “now uses ChatGPT Images 2.5” wording is also not supported by the cited official page. The current OpenAI Help Center calls the product **ChatGPT Images** and separately notes that the official DALL·E GPT has been retired.[1]

## 2. Platform and surface availability

**Stored data: INCORRECT.**

OpenAI explicitly lists ChatGPT Images as available on:

- **Web — available**
- **iOS — available**
- **Android — available**[1]

The stored Windows and macOS entries should not be treated as separately verified native-platform capabilities. The official availability statement identifies **web, iOS, and Android**, rather than confirming dedicated Windows or macOS support.[1]

The current sources do not establish official ChatGPT Images support for:

- **Linux — not verified**
- **Terminal — not verified**
- **Chrome as a separate platform — not verified**

For the **API**, the stored entry is materially outdated. DALL·E 2 and DALL·E 3 were deprecated and removed from the OpenAI API on **May 12, 2026**; developers were directed to use GPT Image models instead.[3][5]

The current Images API documentation lists GPT Image models, including `gpt-image-1`, `gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5`, and newer GPT Image models. It does not list DALL·E as a current model.[3]

## 3. Current status

**Stored data: CORRECT only for the DALL·E-specific feature; incomplete for the replacement product.**

- **Official DALL·E GPT in ChatGPT: Deprecated/retired.**
- **DALL·E API models: Deprecated and removed on May 12, 2026.**[1][3][5]
- **ChatGPT Images: Current available product, not deprecated.** It is the replacement for creating and editing images in ChatGPT.[1]

OpenAI’s current Help Center says: “No—we’ve retired the official DALL·E GPT from ChatGPT. To continue creating or editing images, use ChatGPT Images.”[1]

Therefore, the database should distinguish between:

- `DALL-E Image Generation` — **deprecated**
- `ChatGPT Images` — **available/current**

The cited sources do not characterize ChatGPT Images as Beta, Preview, or invite-only.

## 4. Access gating

**Stored data: INCORRECT.**

The feature is not paid-only. **ChatGPT Images is available on all tiers**, including Free.[1] It is therefore best classified as:

- **Gating:** free with tier-specific usage limits
- **Not:** paid-only
- **Not:** invite-only
- **Not:** organization-only for ordinary ChatGPT Images access

API access is separately usage- and account-controlled. GPT Image API usage is billed according to the selected model and image-generation parameters; some organizations may need verification before using particular models.[14]

## 5. Regional availability

**Stored data: PARTIALLY CORRECT / NOT FULLY VERIFIED.**

OpenAI describes `gpt-image-1` as available globally through the Images API, while noting that some developers may need organization verification.[14] ChatGPT access itself is limited to countries and territories on OpenAI’s supported-countries list; access outside that list can result in blocking or suspension.[12]

Accordingly, “available globally” is acceptable as a broad description of the API’s availability, but it is too absolute for ChatGPT. A more accurate record would be:

> Available in OpenAI-supported ChatGPT countries and territories; API availability is global subject to account, organization-verification, and applicable regional restrictions.

No source identified a new country-specific restriction for ChatGPT Images in the last 30 days.

## 6. Official URL

**Stored data: NOT PROVIDED; add the following official URLs.**

- **ChatGPT Images Help Center:** `https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11084440-images-in-chatgpt`[1]
- **OpenAI Images API reference:** `https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images/methods/generate`[3]
- **OpenAI API deprecations:** `https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations`[8]

The ChatGPT Images Help Center page was active and updated on **October 11, 2026**, so it remains accessible and current.[1]

## 7. Recent changes in the last 30 days

**Stored data: INCORRECT or incomplete because it contains no recent-change record.**

The relevant recent changes are:

- OpenAI’s current Help Center documentation, updated October 11, states that the official DALL·E GPT in ChatGPT has been retired.[1]
- ChatGPT Images is documented as available on all tiers and on web, iOS, and Android.[1]
- OpenAI’s API changelog, updated October 8, reiterates that DALL·E 2 and DALL·E 3 were removed from the API on May 12, 2026 and recommends GPT Image models instead.[5]
- The API reference now lists current GPT Image models rather than DALL·E models for image generation.[3]

There was no cited official announcement in the retrieved material indicating a new image-generation change specifically announced between **September 12 and October 12, 2026**, apart from the updated documentation confirming the current retirement and replacement status.

- Official Help Center: “Deep research in ChatGPT” FAQ (updated ~20 days prior to access; covers usage, limits varying by plan, sources/apps, controls, and regional notes).[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10500283-deep-research-faq)[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10500283-deep-research-faq)
- OpenAI Pricing page (ChatGPT plans: Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business/Enterprise descriptions).[[2]](https://openai.com/pricing)
- “Introducing deep research” announcement page (historical updates through early 2026, including lightweight version rollout).[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-deep-research/)
- API/docs references to deep research models (o3-deep-research, o4-mini-deep-research, and successors) and usage.[[4]](https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing?latest-pricing=batch)[[5]](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/o3-deep-research)
- Recent @OpenAI X posts (no pricing/limit/platform changes noted).[[6]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2067625113193951611)

### Summary of Findings by Category
1. **Pricing changes, new tier availability, or plan restrictions**: No recent changes. Plans match the stored list (Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise). Descriptions note “Limited deep research” (Free/Go), “Expanded deep research” (Plus), and “Maximum deep research” (Pro), with Business/Enterprise using credits or configurable access. Older updates (e.g., April 2025 lightweight o4-mini rollout for higher allowances after full limits) established the full + lightweight structure; current in-product counters handle specifics. Stored limits (e.g., 5/month lightweight for Free/Go; 10+15 for Plus; 125+125 for Pro; custom for Enterprise) are directionally consistent with historical figures (e.g., Free ~5, Plus/Team ~25 total with lightweight component) but not contradicted or precisely restated in latest public pages.[[2]](https://openai.com/pricing)[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-deep-research/)

2. **Platform availability updates**: No changes noted. Available on web, iOS, Android, Windows/macOS desktop apps (as expected from initial rollout notes); unavailable on Linux, Chrome extension (standalone), and terminal. API access exists via dedicated deep research models (e.g., o3-deep-research/o4-mini variants or successors like gpt-5.6-sol in some contexts).[[3]](https://openai.com/index/introducing-deep-research/)

3. **Feature status changes (beta/GA/deprecated)**: Remains GA with detailed Help Center documentation, in-product access (/Deepresearch or tools menu), plan-based usage, connected apps/sources, real-time controls, and report features. No deprecation signals.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10500283-deep-research-faq)

4. **Regional availability**: Availability depends on plan and country/territory (per Help Center). Older rollout notes (e.g., EEA/UK/Switzerland expansions in early 2025) are resolved; no new restrictions or country-specific announcements in recent sources.[[7]](https://help.openai.com/articles/10500283)

5. **Changes in the last 30-60 days**: None identified in official pricing/help/docs or recent @OpenAI posts. February 2026 updates (GPT-5.2 powering, app connections, site restrictions, progress tracking, fullscreen reports) predate the window. June 2026 X posts highlight use cases (e.g., medical research) but no feature/policy shifts. API model references note ongoing support with some legacy deprecation timelines outside the recent period.[[6]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2067625113193951611)

**Overall**: The stored data accurately reflects current GA status, plan gating (with lightweight fallback), and platform support. Limits are presented at a high level in public docs (exact numbers via in-product UI or plan-specific pages), but the structure holds. No evidence of recent disruptions, expansions, or restrictions. For the absolute latest quotas, check in-product counters or logged-in plan details, as they can vary.

Official OpenAI sources (primarily the Help Center article "Projects in ChatGPT," last updated ~21-22 days prior) confirm the feature's general availability (GA) status, broad plan access (including Free), file/project limits by tier, sharing capabilities (with distinctions for Business/Enterprise/Edu), and platform support. No pricing changes, new tier restrictions, deprecation, or major status shifts have occurred. It is included at no extra cost on qualifying plans, with usage charges (e.g., for models/tools) applying the same as regular chats.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt)[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt)

### Key Details Matching Stored Data
- **Plans and gating**: Available to Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu (with sharing on web/mobile). Unlimited projects per user. File limits vary by plan (e.g., Free: 5 per project; Go/Plus: 25; Edu/Pro/Business/Enterprise: 40; max 10 uploaded at once). Sharing/collaboration limits also tiered (e.g., Free: up to 5 collaborators; Pro: up to 100). Business/Enterprise notes on shared projects and admin controls align.[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt)[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt)
- **Platforms**: Confirmed on web (chatgpt.com), iOS/Android mobile apps, and Windows/macOS desktop apps. Linux desktop app is in preview (announced ~August 11, 2026, for specific distros like Ubuntu 24.04/26.04 LTS, Debian 13, Fedora 43/44; .deb/.rpm packages, x64/ARM64), supporting Projects alongside ChatGPT Work and Codex—consistent with the stored ❌ marking for full/GA availability. No support noted for Chrome extension, terminal/CLI (beyond separate tools), or full API access for the ChatGPT Projects feature (API platform has its own separate "projects" for org management, usage tracking, etc.).[[2]](https://www.zdnet.com/article/openai-brings-the-chatgpt-desktop-app-to-linux/)[[3]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2087231350134980830)
- **Feature status**: GA and widely rolled out globally with no noted regional restrictions. Project sharing expanded earlier (to all plans including Free/Go/Plus/Pro by late 2025).[[1]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt)

### Recent Changes (Last ~30-60 Days)
- **August 14, 2026 release notes**: Added ability to switch memory settings (default vs. project-only) on eligible *existing unshared projects* via Project settings (changes may take hours to apply; shared projects remain project-only). Available on all ChatGPT plans. Other minor app updates (e.g., quizzes) noted but unrelated.[[4]](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes)
- **Linux desktop preview (August 11, 2026)**: Extends Projects (plus Work/Codex) to supported Linux systems in preview; worldwide rollout.[[3]](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2087231350134980830)
- No announcements of pricing/plan changes, new restrictions, feature deprecation, or regional rollouts/restrictions in official channels. Earlier expansions (e.g., Free tier access and file limit increases in 2025; shared projects rollout) predate the 30-60 day window.[[5]](https://openai.com/index/more-ways-to-work-with-your-team/)

**Sources cited**: Primary reliance on OpenAI's official Help Center (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10169521-projects-in-chatgpt and translated variants), release notes (https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes), and @OpenAI X posts/announcements. **Stored data: INCORRECT.** The stored Plus/Pro availability is obsolete because Sora itself has been discontinued.

| Plan | Current Sora access | Stored value | Verification |

| Enterprise | ❌ | ❌ | The stored “business version in development” note is outdated; Sora has been discontinued.[1][10] |

**Stored data: INCORRECT.** All listed Sora surfaces should now be marked unavailable or deprecated.

- **Sora discontinuation notice:** `https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001152-what-to-know-about-the-sora-discontinuation`[1]

**Stored data: INCOMPLETE/OUTDATED.**

## 1. Pricing-tier availability and limits

**Stored data: INCORRECT — access is correct, but the notes and limits are outdated.**

| Plan | Access | Current usage treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Yes | Uses the plan’s normal Claude usage limits |
| Pro | Yes | Uses the user’s existing Claude usage limits |
| Max 5x | Yes | Uses the user’s existing Claude usage limits |
| Max 20x | Yes | Uses the user’s existing Claude usage limits |
| Team | Yes | Uses seat/user usage limits; administrators may purchase additional usage credits |
| Enterprise | Yes | Depends on the Enterprise billing model and organization limits |

Anthropic’s current Help Center says Artifacts are available on **Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise** plans.[1] It also states that Artifacts—including designs, decks, and documents—are charged against the user’s existing Claude usage limits; there is **no separate Artifact allocation**.[1]

The stored plan names are therefore correct, but the notes saying that **Design/Slides/Docs are unavailable on Free** are no longer correct. Anthropic’s current product page says **Claude Design, Claude Slides, and Claude Docs are included in every plan, including Free**.[9]

The current feature configuration is:

- **Design, Slides, and Docs:** available on all plans; scheduled to turn on by default on **October 15, 2026**, except in HIPAA-enabled organizations.[1][9]
- **Dashboards:** beta on paid plans—Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise—and disabled until enabled where applicable.[1][9]
- **Motion:** beta on Team and Enterprise plans.[1][9]
- **Enterprise:** owners or administrators control organization-level capabilities; the stored note about templates being off by default is becoming outdated because Design/Slides/Docs are scheduled to turn on by default on October 15, 2026, subject to the stated HIPAA exception.[1][9]

Artifacts also require **Cloud code execution and file creation** to be enabled in the relevant account or organization settings.[1]

## 2. Platform and surface availability

**Stored data: INCORRECT — the broad web/desktop/mobile coverage is right, but terminal and API notes need qualification.**

| Surface | Current availability | Assessment of stored data |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | Yes, through Claude desktop | Correct |
| macOS | Yes, through Claude desktop | Correct |
| Linux | Yes, through Claude desktop | Correct |
| iOS | Yes | Mostly correct; mobile supports requesting, viewing, and editing artifacts |
| Android | Yes | Mostly correct; mobile supports requesting, viewing, and editing artifacts |
| Web | Yes; primary/best-supported surface | Correct |
| Terminal | Yes through Claude Code, subject to plan/login requirements | Stored entry is too broad |
| API | No equivalent end-user Artifacts workspace feature | Mostly correct, but requires qualification |

Anthropic’s current administrator documentation says Artifacts are available in **Claude on the web and desktop**, in **Claude Code**, and through the standalone Claude Design surface.[14] It says iOS and Android users can request an Artifact, view the result, and edit documents, decks, and designs.[14] Thus, the stored mobile note saying that mobile is limited to “view/ask” is outdated because editing is also supported.[14]

Terminal access is not universal across every plan. Current Claude Code documentation indicates that Artifacts in Claude Code require an authenticated session and are available on **Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise** plans.[8] Therefore, the stored statement “terminal: available” should specify the Claude Code plan and authentication requirements rather than implying unrestricted terminal availability.

The stored API entry is directionally correct for the **Claude Artifacts workspace feature**: Artifacts are an application surface rather than a generally available equivalent in the Claude API. However, this should not be interpreted as meaning that no Artifact-related output can ever be generated through developer tools; it means the managed Artifacts experience is not listed as an API-accessible feature.

## 3. Current status

**Stored data: INCORRECT if applied to all Artifact capabilities; otherwise partially correct.**

The core Artifacts feature is a generally available product capability across the listed plans. However, some newer Artifact templates are explicitly **beta**:

- **Dashboards:** beta on paid plans.[1][9]
- **Motion:** beta on Team and Enterprise plans.[1][9]
- **Design, Slides, and Docs:** currently documented as included across plans, with default enablement scheduled for October 15, 2026.[1][9]

Accordingly, the most accurate status field is not simply `ga` for every Artifact-related capability. It should distinguish:

- Core Artifacts: **GA**
- Design/Slides/Docs: **available**, with rollout/default-enablement rules
- Dashboards: **Beta**
- Motion: **Beta**

**Stored data: CORRECT in broad terms, but incomplete.**

Artifacts are **not paid-only** and are not invite-only: the core feature is available on the **Free** plan as well as paid plans.[1][9] The appropriate gating classification remains **free/freemium**, because Free users can access the feature but are subject to Free-plan usage limits.

There are additional capability gates:

- Cloud code execution and file creation must be enabled.[1]
- Some templates are limited to paid plans or particular organization plans—for example, Dashboards and Motion.[1][9]
- Team and Enterprise organizations can restrict sharing and enable or disable capabilities administratively.[9][14]
- Enterprise HIPAA-enabled organizations may have different default settings for Design, Slides, and Docs.[9]

**Stored data: NOT VERIFIED from the retrieved official material.**

The available official results confirm plan and surface availability but do **not** provide a definitive country-by-country statement that Artifacts are available globally. Therefore, “Available globally” should not be treated as fully verified from these sources.

No specific country restriction was identified in the retrieved documentation. However, Claude’s availability generally depends on whether Claude itself is supported in the user’s country or territory, and organization-level policies may further restrict access. The regional field should preferably be recorded as:

> **Available wherever the applicable Claude plan and service are supported; no Artifact-specific country restriction identified.**

That is more precise than an unconditional “available globally.”

The official product page is:

**Claude Artifacts — Claude by Anthropic**[9]

- Change Free-plan notes to indicate that **Design, Slides, and Docs are included**, subject to capability settings and rollout timing.
